questions.q: What two settings must a Key Vault have enabled before it can hold a customer-managed key for storage account encryption?
options: Soft-delete and purge protection
Public network access and anonymous read access
Geo-replication and zone redundancy
Multi-factor authentication and Conditional Access
questions.explain: Azure requires both so the platform has a guarantee the key can't be permanently deleted out from under an encrypted resource.

questions.q: Why does the storage account's managed identity need the Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User role?
options: Without it, the storage account can reference the key but cannot actually use it for encryption
It is required only for soft-delete to function
It grants the storage account permission to delete the vault
It is unrelated to encryption and only controls billing
questions.explain: The role grants the permission to actually use the key for cryptographic operations, which is separate from being able to point at it.

questions.q: How does the order-tracking app retrieve its database connection string after it's moved into Key Vault?
options: Via its own managed identity using DefaultAzureCredential and a SecretClient, or an App Service Key Vault reference
By reading a plain-text value still stored in appsettings.json
By asking another developer to email it the current value
Key Vault pushes the value automatically into source control
questions.explain: The app authenticates with its own identity and retrieves the secret at runtime, so the raw value never has to live in a config file.

questions.q: Why can't Key Vault automatically rotate the database connection string secret the same way it rotates the customer-managed key?
options: Key Vault has no way to generate a new database password on its own, so it can only warn before the current value expires
Secrets are not allowed to have expiration dates in Key Vault
Rotation is only supported for RSA keys, never for text secrets
The connection string is not actually stored in Key Vault
questions.explain: A key rotation policy works because Key Vault can generate a new cryptographic key itself; a secret's actual value has to be rotated by something that understands the target system, like a Function triggered by a near-expiry notification.

questions.q: What problem from Lesson 13 does moving the connection string into Key Vault directly solve?
options: The risk of a hardcoded secret leaking through Git history, build logs, or container image layers
The need to encrypt data at rest on the storage account
The requirement to set up Conditional Access policies
The need for a customer-managed key rotation policy
questions.explain: Lesson 13 warned that a hardcoded secret in a config file or source code leaks through several channels beyond the current file; storing it in Key Vault and reading it at runtime removes all of them.
